key_insight: A continuous-action neurosymbolic RL policy learns investment-mandate compliance, reducing violations to 4.8% without post-hoc action correction.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a way to incorporate regime-dependent allocation rules into portfolio-policy training without requiring an inference-time enforcement layer.
method: Represent a six-rule, regime-conditional investment mandate as symbolic supervision.
Use reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling to estimate the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the mandate.
Add this compliance signal to the continuous-action RL training objective.
evidence_signal: Direct audits of uncorrected deterministic mean actions report 4.8% violations, versus 96–98% for unconstrained RL and 33.4% for a reward-penalty baseline.
watch_item: Compliance is learned rather than guaranteed: residual violations remain, and the abstract does not establish robustness under market distribution shifts.
paper_title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
